name: Reanimated
body:
Not all who die stay dead—but not all who are brought back fully escape death. The reanimated are human (or similar humanoid) bodies that have been brought back to life—but at a cost. Sometimes the usual magic spells and rituals, such as raise dead, didn’t quite work as intended. In other cases, alchemical or scientific experiments were used to try to revivify a body long after it should have been impossible to do so.

Physical

Many reanimated look just like the humans, or other humanoids, that they were in life, although they often look a little worse for the wear—pale, gray, even sickly green.

Some are emaciated, shriveled, desiccated, or rotten, but many are well-enough preserved by alchemical processes to pass for living (if not particularly handsome) beings. In some cases, the body being reanimated is not whole, and so must be completed by sewing on parts from other corpses, riveting on mechanical parts, or even just filling the gaps with straw and mud.

Social

Reanimated form no coherent group. Some seem to be brought back to life by magic invoked by sheer willpower, and retain much of the memories and agendas that drove them in their previous lives. Others are basically pieced together like machines made from the parts of many corpses, and are brought to life with only the most rudimentary understanding of what they are.

Many reanimated feel a kinship to members of fellow misfit species, such as fleshwarps, forgeborn, skeletons, and walking dead.

Alignment And Religion

Many of the reanimated begin as clean-slates, and have a proclivity for neutrality.

Some do remember at least part of their previous lives, or at least the feelings and instincts from those lives, and may have other tendencies. Yet others may feel strange compulsions toward violence, either lashing out like a child because they do not have the tools to more adequately express themselves—or, in more insidious cases, feeling a deep resentment for “natural” living things that they can only express through destruction and murder. Those who fall into this last category, if they do not learn to control such urges, will invariably find themselves on the Evil side of the alignment spectrum.

Religion does not come naturally to the reanimated, and raises more questions among these people than most. Unless they served a deity in their past life, the priesthood is not a common profession for a reanimated, but many of them do eventually find their way to faith on some level.

Names

Some reanimated use the name they had in their previous lives, but for others those memories don’t exist or are a confusing jumble of many different past lives stitched together from the different bodies used to create the reanimated’s new body. For those reanimated who choose a new name for their new life, some typical choices include the following (choose or roll 1d12): 1 Adom, 2 Asher, 3 Caris, 4 Eva, 5 Hann, 6 Hotem, 7 Imman, 8 Leeza, 9 Meela, 10 Prem, 11 Talos, 12 Tera

Standard Species Traits
Ability Score Modifiers You are disoriented and naïve, and your body is stiff and ungainly, but your rebirth has made you uncannily strong. Your ability score modifiers are +4 Str, –2 Dex, –2 Wis [greater paragon]. (2)
Size As a Medium creature, you have no bonuses or penalties due to size. (0)
Type You are a Humanoid with the half-undead and reanimated subtypes. (5)
Speed Your base speed is 30 feet. (0)
Languages You begin play speaking Common. If you have a high Intelligence score, you can choose from any language except for secret languages. (1)
Alternate Species Traits
Darkvision You have darkvision 60 feet. (—)
Half-Undead Traits You gain a +2 species bonus on saving throws against disease and mind-affecting effects. You take no penalties from energy-draining effects, though you can still be killed if you accrue more negative levels than you have Hit Dice. After 24 hours, any negative levels you’ve gained are removed without any additional saving throws. (—)
Negative Energy Affinity You are harmed by positive energy and healed by negative energy. (—)
Past Life Experience Your past life or lives grant you glimpses of knowledge that are eerily intuitive to you in your reanimated life. Pick any one Craft, Knowledge, Perform, or Profession skill. You gain a +2 species bonus on checks with this skill, and that skill is always treated as a class skill for you. (2)
Total: 10 RP (standard)
Alternate Species Traits
Design Beyond Death You had plans and goals while alive, and while the specifics of those may elude you, you find yourself driven even now to achieve some kind of objective. Your ability score modifiers are +2 Wis, +2 Cha. This trait alters ability score modifiers.
Intimidating Your unusual appearance and bearing unnerve those you interact with, giving you a +2 species bonus to Intimidate checks. This trait replaces past life experiences.
Lightning-Born You were brought back to life by experiments involving electricity. You gain electricity resistance 5. In addition, you gain fast healing 2 for 1 round anytime you take electricity damage (whether or not this electricity damage overcomes your electricity resistance). You can heal up to 2 hit points per level per day with this ability, after which it ceases to function. However, the alchemical processes that brought you to life also left you vulnerable to fire; you take an additional +50% more damage from fire attacks and effects than usual. This trait replaces past life experiences.
More Machine Than Man Now In order to be reanimated, large portions of your body has to be replaced with clockwork and other machinery. Instead of the half-undead subtype, you gain the half-construct subtype. You gain a +2 species bonus on saving throws against disease, mind-affecting effects, poison, and effects that cause either exhaustion or fatigue. You cannot be raised or resurrected. You do not breathe, eat, or sleep, unless you want to gain some beneficial effect from one of these activities. (This means that you can drink potions to benefit from their effects and can sleep in order to regain spells, but neither of these activities is required for you to survive or stay in good health.) This trait alters type, and replaces half-undead traits, negative energy affinity, and past life experience.
Mummified While dead, your body underwent special funeral rites and alchemical treatments that still affect you today. You gain a +2 species bonus against poison and death effects, but you suffer a –2 penalty against any spell or effect with the water descriptor. This trait alters half-undead traits.
Slam You can make a slam attack with either or both arms as long as you do not use them to make weapon or claw attacks. These are primary natural attacks that deal 1d4 bludgeoning damage (or 1d3 if you are size Small). This trait replaces darkvision.
Small You have been reanimated from a Small-sized humanoid, such as a halfling. You are size Small, and your ability score modifiers are +2 Str, +2 Con, –2 Wis. This trait alters size and ability score modifiers.
Unnatural You unnerve normal animals, and train to defend yourself against the inevitable attacks from such creatures. You take a –4 penalty on all Charisma-based skill checks to affect creatures of the animal type, and receive a +4 dodge bonus to AC against animals. Animals’ starting attitude toward you is one step worse than normal. This trait replaces past life experiences.
Feats
Reanimated Surgery

You understand how to repair damage to reanimated bodies.

Prerequisite(s): Heal 1 rank, Knowledge (arcana) 1 rank.

Benefit(s): Once per day, you can reattach a reanimated’s severed limb, or attach a similarly-sized limb from a different, recently-deceased humanoid. Alternately, you can use this feat to restore 1d4 points of ability damage to one of a reanimated’s physical ability scores (Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution). Using this feat requires 1 hour. You can only use it on reanimated; you can use it on yourself if you are reanimated.

Alternative Favored Class Bonuses
Alchemist Add +1/4 to your natural armor bonus when using your mutagen.
Barbarian Add +1 to your total number of rage rounds per day
Bard Treat your effective bard level as +1/2 level higher for the purpose of determining the effect of the fascinate bardic performance.
Cleric Add +1/4 to your caster level when determining the effects of your domain spells cast with domain spell slots.
Fighter Choose the bull rush or overrun combat maneuver. Add +1/3 to your CMB when attempting this maneuver (maximum bonus of +4).
Gunslinger Add +1/4 to your grit points.
Mesmerist When casting mesmerist enchantment spells, add +1/2 to your effective caster level, but only to determine the spell’s duration.
Monk Add +1 to your CMD when resisting a grapple and +1/2 to the number of stunning attacks you can attempt per day.
Occultist Gain +1/6 of a new focus power.
Oracle Add one spell known from the oracle spell list. This spell must be at least one spell level below the highest-level oracle spell you can cast.
Psychic Gain +1/6 of a new phrenic amplification.
Sorcerer Select one bloodline power at 1st level that is normally usable a number of times equal to 3 + your Charisma modifier. Add + 1/2 to the number of uses per day of that bloodline power.
Summoner Your eidolon gain resistance 1 against either cold or electricity. Each time you select this reward, you increase your eidolon’s resistance to one of those energy types by 1 (maximum 10 for any one energy type).
Vigilante Add +1/2 to the DC increase from unshakable.
Witch Add one spell from the witch spell list to your familiar. This spell must be at least one spell level below the highest-level witch spell you can cast. If you ever replace your familiar, the new familiar knows these bonus spells.
